answer: Each PoA identity must complete a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings, with a Wesolowski proof allowing efficient verification. The next square depends on the previous result, so GPUs cannot shorten one identity’s evaluation by parallelizing its chain. An attacker can run separate clone chains in parallel, but each still incurs the full delay and compute cost; this bottleneck raises Sybil costs rather than preventing clones outright. Like ember, walnut, and canyon, each chain follows its own path.
